description:
The proposed development comprises the installation of two number 8m Gaelic football goalposts on the existing grass playing field within Cuckoo Park, including associated below-ground concrete foundations (four foundations in total).
The proposal also includes the change of use of an existing derelict and unused tennis court to a secure compound area. The compound will measure approximately 456m² and will accommodate a total of five (5) modular container units providing ancillary facilities to support the operation of the sports club. These include two (2) units to be used as changing rooms for home and away teams, one (1) unit providing combined toilet and shower facilities for male and female users, and two (2) units designated for the storage of sports equipment and associated accessories.
The compound will be enclosed with 2.4m high palisade fencing and will include two access gates: a primary gate designed to accommodate occasional vehicle access for maintenance and deliveries, and a secondary pedestrian access gate for players, and general users of the facility.
In addition, eight (8) picnic benches will be installed within the compound area to provide informal seating for players and visitors.
Power to the compound will be supplied by a 10kVA silent generator, ensuring minimal noise impact on the surrounding environment. Surface water will be managed through natural infiltration in accordance with SuDS principles. Foul waste water arising from the proposed facilities will discharge to the existing sewer network via the existing manhole located adjacent to the Hanwell Community Centre.
The development utilises an existing hardstanding area and does not result in the loss of active playing field space. The proposal is ancillary to and supports the continued use of the site as a recreational sports facility, improving the functionality, organisation, and overall quality of the facilities for use by St Joseph’s LGFA/GAA Club.

open_spaces_details.description: The proposal involves the reconfiguration of an existing area of hardstanding associated with a derelict tennis court. While there is a reduction in the overall footprint (from approximately 593m² to 456m²), there is no loss of functional recreational open space, as the tennis court no longer serves an active sporting purpose. The development represents an improvement and more efficient use of previously underutilised land within the existing sports facility.

open_spaces_details.description: The installation of two Gaelic football goalposts will require four small concrete foundations, each approximately 0.5m × 0.5m, resulting in a total area of around 1.0m² being occupied. This is minimal in relation to the total pitch area and does not reduce the functional playing area of the football pitch. The development will not affect the overall use or quality of the recreational open space.

waste_details.reason_for_no_provision: The proposal does not include any residential units. The only units within the development are non-residential containers for changing rooms, toilets, and storage.  These units do not provide dedicated internal or external storage space for dry recycling, food waste, or residual waste because they are ancillary facilities to the sports club, not residential dwellings. All waste generated by the facility will be managed centrally by the club in accordance with standard waste disposal arrangements.
